A 28-year-old male seeks emergency care for arm pain following a recent open radius fracture that
occurred during a fall from a ladder at home. After undergoing open reduction and internal fixation and
cast placement, he has experienced progressive arm pain. His medical history includes hypertension
and asthma, with current medications including albuterol, fluticasone, loratadine, and lisinopril. Vital
signs show temperature 97.2°F (37.5°C), blood pressure 133/92 mmHg, pulse 61/min, respirations
16/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. Upon cast removal and examination, his left arm
shows tenderness to palpation, severe pain with passive movement of wrist and fingers, palpable radial
and ulnar pulses, and a firm, tender forearm without bruising. What is the most appropriate next step in
management? Answer Choices: (A) Administration of IV antibiotics (B) Doppler ultrasound of the arm
(C) Radiography (D) Immediate MRI of the forearm (E) Surgical hardware removal (F) CT angiography
of the arm (G) Compartment pressure measurement (H) Replace the cast with a sling (I) Pain
management and observation (J) Emergency fasciotomy
 A. Doppler ultrasound of the arm
B. Replace the cast with a sling
C. Surgical hardware removal
D. CT angiography of the arm
E. Pain management and observation
F. Administration of IV antibiotics
G. Immediate MRI of the forearm

H. Emergency fasciotomy
I. Radiography
J. Compartment pressure measurement
